resources.string: Find the bass values for this phone\'s speaker by ear. Takes about 10 minutes.
Find the bass for this phone
By ear, find how low the speaker goes, how much virtual bass to add, and where it starts to buzz. The order of the questions and the A/B sides change every time.
Set your usual listening volume. If the volume changes during the test, it pauses.
Listen in a quiet place, on the phone\'s speaker, holding the phone as usual.
Nothing changes until you save, and you can undo it afterwards.
Available while Rootnote is on and sound comes from the phone\'s speaker.
Back to the values before the fit
The phone\'s microphone compares the room with the check sound. Nothing is saved.
The room is noisy, so the result may be off! Go on anyway?
Tightest band %1$d Hz · margin %2$d dB (%3$d dB needed)
The room level jumps (%1$d dB, %2$d dB or less needed)
The microphone isn\'t available, so the room can\'t be measured. Go on anyway?
Step 1 · The lowest sound the speaker plays
The sound plays in one of two turns, and sometimes in neither. If you heard no note, only a rattle or noise, choose \"Only buzz\".
First part: one middle note that gets quieter, to find how faintly you hear at this volume.
Second part: lower and lower notes, each a little louder than you just barely heard.
A sound in the room got in, so the same question plays again
Is X the same as A or as B?
Play A, B and X as often as you like. If you can\'t tell, a guess is fine.
One of the two has the virtual bass off.
One of the two makes harmonics up to a higher note.
Play A and B, then choose. If you can\'t hear a difference, choose \"No difference\".
Does the bass rattle or buzz?

Answer about the \"Bass\" clip. Clean: only the bass note, smooth. A hum you feel in your hand is still clean. Rattles: a \"brrr\", clattering sound added on the beat, as if something loose touches and shakes along. Buzzes: the sound itself cracks or tears. \"Reference\" plays the same clip with the virtual bass off: compare with it. Some questions have the virtual bass off.
Some questions with the virtual bass off also rattled or buzzed: the volume alone is too high for this speaker. Lower it and run again.
Compare 18 pairs to choose the harmonics\' slope and the weight of the lowest one. About 5 more minutes.
The volume changed. Set it back to where you started (%1$s).
Switch back to the phone\'s speaker.
Rootnote isn\'t processing the sound. Turn it on again.
Couldn\'t be told from off at this volume
Measured in a noisy room. Treat it as a rough guide.
Nothing to change: what the test found is the same as now, or not reliable enough to apply.
Play some music and switch between 1 and 2. One is your current settings, the other the new ones.
You chose the new settings %2$d of %1$d times.
Your current settings sounded better. Not saving is recommended.
You can see and change the values in developer mode. If you don\'t like them, use \"Undo the last fit\" in Bass fit.
Measuring the speaker\'s bass with the microphone (reference)
Measured with the phone\'s microphone · reference, not applied
The floor you found by ear is more than 1/3 octave below the microphone\'s. You may have heard a rattle or body vibration as the note.
The floor you found by ear is more than 1/3 octave above the microphone\'s. The volume may be low, or room sound may have covered it.
Repeat one step several times to compare it with a measuring microphone (UMIK-1) or to check how well it repeats. Nothing is applied; every run goes to a log (CSV).
The conditions that are on come in a random order, without saying which. %1$d runs in all. The room is checked once at the start.
Turn on the RTA in REW on the PC and put the UMIK-1 where your ears are. Each condition plays 20 s of pink noise, then a 10 s sweep while the phone microphone\'s value is logged.
Pink noise · measure with REW\'s RTA
All %1$d rows will be deleted. This can\'t be undone.
Take a short break if you like. Keep the volume where it is.
